name: pedal-power
title: Pedal power entry: 9 V centre-negative jack, Schottky, 100 Ω / 100 µF, 4.5 V reference
about: A pedal's 9 V input: a 5.5 mm DC jack wired centre negative, an SS14 Schottky in the plus leg against a reversed plug, then 100 Ω and 100 µF as the filter of the audio rail, and the reference at half that rail – two 10 kΩ with 100 µF. The parts are rated for a 12 or 18 V outlet as well (jack 24 V, diode 40 V, capacitors 35 V). Maker-coverage BL-17.

ports.vplus: the protected supply behind the diode, unfiltered: relay coils, LEDs, a regulator for the logic
ports.out: the filtered rail for the audio stages (op-amp supplies)
ports.vref: half of out (4.5 V at 9 V): the bias of the audio stages

components.label: {as}: 9 V DC jack, centre negative (pin 1 ground, pin 2 plus)
components.notes: Centre negative: pin 1 (centre) ground, pin 2 (barrel) plus. Pin 3, the switch lug, is closed to pin 2 without a plug – battery plus there, else in nc.

components.label: {as}: reverse-polarity Schottky in the plus leg

nets.name: jack
nets.notes: The jack's plus (barrel contact): a reversed plug reaches D1's anode only.

notes: J1 centre negative, the pedal convention (HINT.pedal_supply): pin 1 (the 2.0 mm centre pin) ground, pin 2 plus. J1 carries "source": "reversible": PATH.reverse checks that a centre-positive plug reaches only D1's anode. Check that the adapter's plug fits the 2.0 mm pin.

D1 SS14 in the plus leg – not in the ground leg, which the audio cables' shields bypass (HINT.pedal_supply): 40 V reverse, so a reversed 18 V outlet stays within 0.67 × 40 V = 26.8 V; 1 A; VF ≤ 0.55 V at 1 A (MDD SS12…SS1200, Rev 2025A5). The library's AO3401A (block reverse-pmos) would drop less, but its gate allows ±12 V only – a 12 V outlet is at its limit, an 18 V one beyond.

R1 100 Ω and C1 100 µF: the audio rail's low-pass at 1/(2π · 100 Ω · 100 µF) = 15.9 Hz. R1 drops 0.1 V per mA (1 V at 10 mA, maker-coverage GTP 34) and carries 25 mA at most (0805, 1/8 W, 50 % derating): relay coils, LEDs and a logic regulator go on vplus, ahead of R1.

R2, R3 10 kΩ and C2 100 µF: vref at half of out with 5 kΩ source resistance – loads on vref at least 50 kΩ, 10 × the divider (maker-coverage GTP 9); megohm bias resistors are far above. τ = 5 kΩ × 100 µF = 0.5 s: vref ramps up over about 2.5 s at power-on (the thump of GTP 9 is that ramp). C2 is the same part as C1 – more than the 10 µF the reference needs at least, one part fewer. The divider draws 0.45 mA at 9 V.
C1, C2 35 V: an 18 V outlet stays within 0.67 × 35 V = 23.5 V (maker-coverage GTP 36). The nets are declared up to 18 V (vref 9 V) – for 9 V supplies only, narrow them.
Battery: its plus on J1 pin 3 (remove it from nc), so the adapter's plug cuts it off; its minus through the input jack's ring contact (HINT.jack_battery).
sim.json: J1 under sources (plus "2", minus "1") with the outlet's current limit as i_max_a, and its voltages under supplies (e.g. 8.5, 9, 9.6 V).
A bulk capacitor on vplus as well where relay coils or LEDs switch there (HINT.bulk).

test.about: vplus, out and vref become the nets T_VPLUS, T_OUT and T_VREF; the jack J1 becomes J2 – a 9 V source beside the example's 5 V J1

J2.note: values for the test: a 9 V outlet of a pedal supply, not a data sheet's
